title: Reed section in the Louis Russell band
summary: Nicholas's alto and tenor chairs, the band's trumpets and trombone, and playing sax in a section.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Did you, well which sax did you play with, say Louis Russell?

I played third alto. I played first alto. Charlie Holmes was on third. And Tenny Hill when I joined the band in 29, was on tenor. Then later on we had two tenors and two altos. I played for about two years alto. Then it changed me to tenor. And I played first tenor when Greely Walton came in the band. I was playing alto when Greely came. Then we marched in the band with four, with four. And Louis came in the band. Then I went on first tenor. I played until 1940. I'd switch up and down. Sometime I'd play alto, sometime I'd play that. Then I played baritone sax also. I played baritone. And all the clarinet worked got just for me in the band. And we had three other trumpets besides Louis. We had Red Island, Otis Johnson, and Hemp Hill, and Louis. It was four trumpets, three trumpets. We had Higginbottom, George Washington, very good trumpets. And the Paris, Sidney the Paris. I know, Wilbur the Paris.
That's not the same George Washington that was down here in New Orleans.
I don't know, he was in New York.
It was a real short little George Washington that used to play with Buddy Petit. No, no, no.

That's another guy. He was a good arranger also. He used to arrange for us in the band. We had a couple of rangers in the band. George Washington was a good arranger. He played a pretty good straight trombone. He wasn't going to get off man, you know. But he played the notes right.
Did you stick mostly to the sax then or did you switch your arms?

No, I switched when I'm playing clarinet. But no, you had to play sax in those days to stay with the band. All the range, you had to play exactly what was written. Only when you take it solo that you play with your field and the band.
Yeah, you know, you play a large solo. Yeah.
